subject: physics
pattern: Electromagnetic Induction carries roughly 8 to 11 marks: a 1-mark law or definition, 2-mark numericals on induced emf, a 3-mark derivation (motional emf, solenoid self inductance, energy in an inductor) and often a 5-mark derivation of the emf of an AC generator or mutual inductance of coaxial solenoids. Examiners expect Faraday's and Lenz's laws stated exactly, the direction of induced current justified, and SI units given.

questions.q: State Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction.
questions.answer: The magnitude of the emf induced in a circuit is equal to the rate of change of magnetic flux through the circuit: $\varepsilon = -N\frac{d\phi}{dt}$, where the negative sign indicates the direction as per Lenz's law.
The direction of the induced emf (and current) is such that it opposes the change in magnetic flux that produces it.

questions.q: Define magnetic flux. Write its SI unit.
questions.answer: Magnetic flux through a surface is the total number of magnetic field lines passing normally through it: $\phi = \vec{B}\cdot\vec{A} = BA\cos\theta$. SI unit: weber (Wb) = T m$^2$.

questions.q: Define self-inductance. Write its SI unit and define one henry.
questions.answer: Self-inductance of a coil is the ratio of the magnetic flux linked with it to the current flowing through it: $L = \frac{N\phi}{I}$, equivalently $\varepsilon = -L\frac{dI}{dt}$. SI unit: henry (H). One henry is the self-inductance of a coil in which a current changing at 1 A per second induces an emf of 1 V.

questions.q: What are eddy currents? Mention two applications.
questions.answer: Eddy currents are the circulating currents induced in a bulk piece of conductor when the magnetic flux through it changes. Applications: (i) electromagnetic damping in galvanometers and balances, (ii) induction furnaces for melting metals, (iii) magnetic braking in trains, (iv) electric power meters. They are reduced in transformer cores by laminating the core. (Any two applications.)

questions.q: The magnetic flux through a coil of 100 turns changes from 0.02 Wb to 0.01 Wb in 0.1 s. Find the magnitude of the induced emf.
Mention two factors on which the self-inductance of a long solenoid depends.
questions.answer: For a long solenoid $L = \mu_0\mu_rn^2Al$, so it depends on: (i) the number of turns per unit length n (and total turns), (ii) the area of cross-section A and length l, and (iii) the permeability of the core material (a soft-iron core increases L). (Any two.)

questions.q: Derive an expression for the motional emf induced in a conductor of length l moving with velocity v perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field B.
questions.answer: A rod PQ of length l slides with velocity v on a U-shaped conducting frame in a field B perpendicular to the plane. Let x be the distance of the rod from the closed end. Flux through the loop $\phi = Blx$. Induced emf $\varepsilon = -\frac{d\phi}{dt} = -Bl\frac{dx}{dt}$. Since $\frac{dx}{dt} = v$, magnitude $\varepsilon = Blv$. Alternatively, force on free electrons in the rod is $evB$ and they accumulate at one end until the electric force balances it; the work done per unit charge over length l gives $\varepsilon = Blv$. The direction is given by Fleming's right-hand rule (Lenz's law).

questions.q: Derive an expression for the self-inductance of a long air-cored solenoid.
questions.answer: Consider a solenoid of length l, area A, with n turns per unit length (total N = nl) carrying current I. Field inside: $B = \mu_0nI$. Flux through one turn $= BA = \mu_0nIA$. Flux linkage for all turns $N\phi = (nl)(\mu_0nIA) = \mu_0n^2AlI$. Since $N\phi = LI$, $L = \mu_0n^2Al$. If the core has relative permeability $\mu_r$, $L = \mu_0\mu_rn^2Al$.

questions.q: Show that Lenz's law is in accordance with the law of conservation of energy.
questions.answer: Suppose the north pole of a bar magnet is pushed towards a closed coil. By Lenz's law the induced current flows so that the near face of the coil becomes a north pole, repelling the magnet. Work must therefore be done against this opposing force to push the magnet in, and this mechanical work appears as electrical energy in the coil, finally dissipated as heat ($I^2R$). If the induced current had instead made the near face a south pole, the magnet would be pulled in and would accelerate, gaining kinetic energy while also producing electrical energy without any work done: this would create energy from nothing, violating conservation of energy. Hence the opposing nature of the induced emf is a consequence of energy conservation.
keywords: converted to electrical energy and heat

questions.q: A metal rod of length 0.5 m moves with a speed of 4 m s$^{-1}$ perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.2 T. Calculate the induced emf. If the rod forms part of a closed circuit of total resistance 2 $\Omega$, find the induced current.
questions.answer: Motional emf $\varepsilon = Blv = 0.2\times0.5\times4 = 0.4$ V. Current $I = \frac{\varepsilon}{R} = \frac{0.4}{2} = 0.2$ A.

questions.q: Derive an expression for the energy stored in an inductor carrying a current I.
questions.answer: While the current in a coil of self-inductance L increases, the induced emf opposes it: $\varepsilon = -L\frac{dI}{dt}$. The source must do work against this emf. Power supplied $P = |\varepsilon|I = LI\frac{dI}{dt}$. Work done in time dt: $dW = LI\,dI$. Total work to raise the current from 0 to I: $W = \int_0^ILI\,dI = \frac{1}{2}LI^2$. This is stored as magnetic energy: $U = \frac{1}{2}LI^2$. Energy density of the magnetic field is $\frac{B^2}{2\mu_0}$.

questions.q: Obtain an expression for the emf induced in a coil rotating in a uniform magnetic field (AC generator). State the principle of the AC generator.
questions.answer: Principle: electromagnetic induction; an emf is induced when the flux linked with a coil changes by rotating it in a magnetic field. Construction: a coil (armature) of N turns and area A rotates with angular velocity $\omega$ between the poles of a strong magnet; its ends are connected to slip rings and carbon brushes. Derivation: let the normal to the coil make angle $\theta = \omega t$ with B at time t. Flux $\phi = NBA\cos\omega t$. Induced emf $\varepsilon = -\frac{d\phi}{dt} = NBA\omega\sin\omega t$. Hence $\varepsilon = \varepsilon_0\sin\omega t$ with peak value $\varepsilon_0 = NBA\omega$. The emf is alternating (sinusoidal) with frequency $\nu = \frac{\omega}{2\pi}$; it is maximum when the coil plane is parallel to B and zero when it is perpendicular to B. The output current is $I = I_0\sin\omega t$.
keywords: emf = NBA omega sin omega t

questions.q: Define mutual inductance. Derive an expression for the mutual inductance of two long coaxial solenoids.
questions.answer: Mutual inductance of two coils is the magnetic flux linked with one coil per unit current in the other: $\phi_2 = MI_1$, or emf induced $\varepsilon_2 = -M\frac{dI_1}{dt}$; SI unit henry. Derivation: let a long solenoid S1 (radius $r_1$, $n_1$ turns per unit length, length l) be surrounded by a coaxial solenoid S2 of the same length with $n_2$ turns per unit length. Current $I_2$ in S2 gives a field $B_2 = \mu_0n_2I_2$ inside, so the flux through each turn of S1 is $B_2\pi r_1^2 = \mu_0n_2I_2\pi r_1^2$. Flux linkage with S1 ($N_1 = n_1l$ turns): $N_1\phi_1 = n_1l\,\mu_0n_2I_2\pi r_1^2$. Since $N_1\phi_1 = M_{12}I_2$, $M = \mu_0n_1n_2\pi r_1^2l$. The same value is obtained for $M_{21}$, so $M_{12} = M_{21}$. With a core of relative permeability $\mu_r$, M is multiplied by $\mu_r$.
keywords: M = mu0 n1 n2 pi r1^2 l
